text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should add a persistent skip link at the top of every page that jumps to the main content, because this allows keyboard users to bypass repetitive navigation and quickly access the main content. This decision prioritizes keyboard navigation over a cleaner visual design, which is a trade-off I'm accepting because keyboard accessibility is crucial for users with mobility impairments. By doing this, we ensure that all users can efficiently navigate the website, regardless of their abilities. This decision also sets a strong foundation for further accessibility improvements, such as enhanced screen reader support and improved contrast ratios.

name: Reader
text: A persistent skip link hides the bypass option from sighted keyboard users unless they tab through the entire navigation first—defeating its purpose. Instead, make the skip link visible on focus only, so it appears when needed but doesn’t clutter the interface. Settle this by testing with a screen reader and keyboard user: if they can’t reach the skip link within three tabs, the design fails.

name: Ramp
text:
We should make the skip link visible only on keyboard focus, so it appears when needed but doesn't clutter the interface. This decision prioritizes simplicity and minimalism in our visual design, while still providing essential functionality for keyboard users. By doing this, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially confusing sighted keyboard users who aren't familiar with keyboard navigation, but this is outweighed by the benefits of a cleaner design and improved usability for screen reader users. This approach also aligns with the principle of providing a quality-first experience, as it ensures that our interface is both functional and visually appealing.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is that a focus-only skip link still hides the bypass option from users who don't know to expect it, causing frustration for those who need it most. A better alternative is to use a visible skip link that is discreetly placed, such as in the top-right corner, allowing users to easily find and use it without cluttering the main interface. This argument can be settled by conducting usability testing with a diverse group of users, including those with disabilities, to see which approach is most effective and user-friendly.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Use a discreet but always-visible skip link (e.g., top-right icon) that expands on focus, tested with screen readers and keyboard users. Deliver: working skip link component + test report. Owner: Ramp.
